title: DynaCrys: Crystal Generation with Dynamic Space-Group Diffusion
abstract:
arXiv:2608.07401v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The search for new crystalline materials spans an enormous compositional and structural space. Generating candidates in this space requires modeling the relationships between elemental composition, crystallographic symmetry, and crystal geometry. The space group specifies the crystal's symmetry and determines the admissible Wyckoff positions and geometric degrees of freedom; fixing it in advance prevents this global symmetry choice from being revised using information from evolving Wyckoff occupations and elemental composition. We introduce DynaCrys, the first framework for complete crystal generation in which the space group co-evolves with Wyckoff occupations and elements. We develop physics-informed space-group diffusion that explicitly incorporates crystallographic group-subgroup relations, and a legality-constrained stochastic decoder that jointly samples compatible space groups, Wyckoff occupations, and elements, followed by symmetry-constrained geometry generation. In large-scale evaluations on standard benchmarks, DynaCrys achieves state-of-the-art performance in symmetry-aware crystal generation while supporting fast sampling.
relevance_reason: Key author: Boris Kozinsky

title: FrOGS: Discrete Neural Sampler for Independent Alloy Configurations Across Chemical Conditions
abstract:
arXiv:2609.02948v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Predicting the thermodynamic properties of an alloy requires sampling its configurations across many chemical conditions and recovering free energies on a common absolute scale. Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) is the standard tool, but it requires separate simulations at different conditions, and auxiliary free-energy methods such as thermodynamic integration are used to place results on a common absolute scale. Modern discrete neural samplers typically use reverse KL divergence as the objective and can be mode-seeking or biased. We present Free energy Offering Generative Sampler (FrOGS), a hybrid discrete neural sampler that couples an autoregressive model to a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) to be trained jointly under a single shared loss. FrOGS draws i.i.d. configurations, returns an unbiased estimate of the partition function, and gives consistent estimates of thermodynamic observables. We train a single model across a wide range of chemical conditions to produce estimates on a common absolute free-energy scale. FrOGS matches exact finite-size results on the 2D Ising model and reference phase diagrams for AgPd and CuAu, without mode collapse. We additionally compare to SEGAL, a published autoregressive baseline, and find that only FrOGS recovers the stability range of the CuAu$_3$ phase.
relevance_reason: Key author: Tess Smidt

title: A high-dimensional neural network potential for finite-temperature phenomena in NiTi martensite
authors: J\"{o}rg Behler (Lehrstuhl f\"{u}r Theoretische Chemie II
abstract:
arXiv:2607.20681v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present a high-dimensional neural network potential (HDNNP) for the martensitic phase of the NiTi shape-memory alloy trained to density functional theory (DFT) data. A central aspect of this work is the systematic validation of the potential with respect to the underlying DFT reference method for key properties governing structural evolution, including equilibrium crystal structures, elastic constants, generalized-stacking fault energies, and vibrational spectra. The HDNNP accurately describes the relative stability of the B19$^\prime$ and B33 phases, including subtle energy differences on the order of meV/atom. The predicted stacking-fault energy landscape is strongly anisotropic and reveals a preferential shear pathway, providing atomistic insight into deformation and twinning mechanisms. Finite-temperature molecular dynamics simulations further enable the investigation of unconstrained structural evolution as a function of temperature. Overall, the developed HDNNP provides a robust basis for atomistic simulations of the complex structural and functional behavior of martensitic NiTi systems containing hundreds of thousands of atoms on nanosecond time scales.
relevance_reason: A high-dimensional neural network potential trained on DFT data and validated against DFT for NiTi martensite (elastic constants, stacking faults, phonons) plus finite-temperature MD, satisfying (a), (b) and (c).

title: How anion composition governs structural frameworks and Li-ion transport in oxychloride solid-state electrolytes
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13611v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mixed-anion lithium oxychlorides exhibit high Li conductivity, but the relationship between oxygen content, structural framework, and Li-ion transport remains unclear. Here, crystal structure prediction and molecular dynamics simulations with machine-learning interatomic potentials are used to examine $\mathrm{Li}_yM\mathrm{O}_x\mathrm{Cl}_{6-2x}$ ($M$ = Nb and Ta [Group 5] and $M$ = Ti, Zr, and Hf [Group 4]). Increasing oxygen content changes isolated chloride-rich polyhedra into one-dimensional chains and subsequently more highly connected two- and three-dimensional frameworks. In the Group 5 series, fast Li diffusion occurs over $x \approx 0.67$--1.5, where the Li sites form a three-dimensional percolating network. Potential of mean force maps and nudged elastic band calculations reveal that fast Li-ion transport requires a low-dimensional framework supporting long-range migration through undercoordinated Li sites with low barriers, together with similar energies across Li sites. Finally, we perform fine-grid compositional search, which identifies $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{0.67}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.67}$, $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{0.75}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.5}$, $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$, and $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$ as stable candidates with predicted room-temperature self-diffusivities of up to $\sim 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{cm}^2/\mathrm{s}$. These findings establish how oxygen content controls framework and Li-ion transport, guiding the design of lithium oxyhalide electrolytes.
relevance_reason: MLIP-driven crystal structure prediction and MD with PMF/NEB for Li oxychlorides; explicit atoms, MLIP/MD/NEB, and materials application satisfy (a)-(c).

title: A domain-specific atomistic model for Earth's core materials
abstract:
arXiv:2611.12919v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Understanding Earth's core requires accurate descriptions of multicomponent iron alloys under extreme conditions. Here, we develop the Earth's Core Atomistic Model (ECAM) for Fe-Ni-S-Si-O-C-H alloys through sampling with a foundational atomistic model, targeted ab initio simulations, and iterative exploration. A compact dataset selected from nearly half a million configurations is consistently labeled using high-accuracy first-principles calculations and used to train a lightweight model. The model explicitly includes thermal electronic contributions and runs nearly two orders of magnitude faster than the original foundational model. ECAM corrects artifacts in the foundational model's description of core materials and reproduces the density, seismic velocity, Gibbs free energy, and phase diagrams of Fe and binary alloys in agreement with previous ab initio calculations. ECAM is expected to enable more realistic modeling of chemical partitioning and crystallization in Earth's core. Our workflow also provides a practical route from foundational-model sampling to efficient domain-specific simulation.
relevance_reason: Development of a domain-specific machine-learned interatomic potential (ECAM) for Fe-Ni-S-Si-O-C-H alloys trained on ab initio labels and used in atomistic simulation of density, seismic velocities and phase diagrams, satisfying (a), (b) and (c).

title: Point defects and primary radiation damage in Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn high-entropy alloys from molecular dynamics
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13038v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are candidates for nuclear structural applications. We used molecular dynamics with the EAM-21 potential, stiffened at short range, to study five HEAs that have been irradiated experimentally: Fe37Ni34Cr16Mn13 (ES1), Fe35Ni35Cr15Mn15 (P35), Fe46Ni22Cr15Mn17 (Y3), Fe27Ni28Cr18Mn27 (Kumar) and Fe30Ni30Cr10Mn30 (C30). They were compared with pure Ni, Fe60Ni40, the Fe70Ni10Cr20 model alloy of 316L, and Fe50Ni34Cr16, which is ES1 with Mn replaced by Fe. We calculated stacking fault energies, threshold displacement energies, point-defect formation and migration energies, and 1015 displacement cascades from 5 to 40 keV at 300 and 823 K. The stacking fault energy follows the Ni content: 19-44 mJ/m^2 in the alloys and 113 mJ/m^2 in Ni. Compared with the Mn-free alloys, the HEAs have lower threshold displacement energies (48-56 against 64-74 eV) and lower dumbbell formation energies, and Mn is the element most transported by interstitials. All the concentrated alloys leave about the same number of Frenkel pairs, 56-72 at 40 keV, half the number in Ni. At 40 keV, 54-58% of the interstitials are in clusters in the HEAs, against 67-71% in Fe60Ni40, Fe70Ni10Cr20 and Fe50Ni34Cr16 and 82% in Ni. At the same cluster size, clusters of 4-12 interstitials are faulted about half as often in the HEAs, and this does not follow the stacking fault energy. The surviving interstitials are enriched in Mn in the HEAs and in Ni in the Mn-free alloys, and depleted in Cr. The results support direct loop formation in cascades in Fe60Ni40 and Fe70Ni10Cr20 and less of it in ES1.
relevance_reason: Classical molecular dynamics with the EAM-21 potential (stiffened short-range) applied to displacement cascades, defect energetics and migration in Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn high-entropy alloys — explicit atoms (a), classical force field plus MD (b), and an applied simulation study (c) all clearly satisfied.

title: Orchestr.AI: A Unified Workflow for Training and Benchmarking of Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13898v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Machine-learning force fields enable atomistic simulations at near-reference accuracy and substantially reduced computational cost, but their development remains fragmented across software frameworks with incompatible data formats, configuration schemes, dependencies, and execution procedures. Orchestr.AI addresses this limitation through a unified workflow that coordinates different MLIP software frameworks, referred to as engines, for data preparation, model training, fine-tuning, evaluation, and deployment. A common YAML interface defines each experiment, while engine-specific environment profiles preserve compatible software stacks and avoid dependency conflicts. The platform currently supports five MLIP model architectures, namely SchNet, PaiNN, NequIP, Allegro, and MACE, through their corresponding software implementations, providing automated configuration mapping and standardized dataset handling across these frameworks. Benchmarks on the rMD17 and 3BPA datasets show that Orchestr.AI reproduces the expected performance trends while enabling controlled cross-engine comparisons. Repeated executions with fixed configurations and engine profiles produce highly consistent results, demonstrating practical workflow reproducibility. Beyond training, Orchestr.AI provides modular architectural interfaces that connect trained models to ASE-based simulations, batch inference, epistemic uncertainty estimation, calibration, and active-learning workflows. The platform therefore provides a reproducible and extensible infrastructure for developing, comparing, and deploying machine-learning interatomic potentials, which we validate here through cross-engine accuracy and repeatability benchmarks.
relevance_reason: Unified workflow for training and benchmarking MLIPs (SchNet, PaiNN, NequIP, Allegro, MACE) on rMD17/3BPA; explicit-atom MLIP development satisfies (a)-(c).

title: Development of reactive force field for Pd–Zn system and kinetic study of diffusion-driven alloy formation
abstract: PdZn alloys are catalysts for many reactions, and the 1:1 tetragonal PdZn intermetallic compound has been identified as the active phase for methanol steam reforming (MSR), a crucial process in hydrogen production. Yet, the mechanism and kinetics of the formation of PdZn alloys have not been addressed theoretically. In this work, reactive force field (ReaxFF) parameters for the Pd–Zn system were developed using density functional theory (DFT) training sets generated with the aid of structure prediction and DFT calculations, and the alloying process of Pd and Zn metals was investigated by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. MD simulations of Pd@Zn and Zn@Pd core–shell models revealed a two-stage, diffusion-controlled alloying process with distinct diffusion coefficients and activation energies for Pd and Zn atoms, and a kinetic model was proposed for the fast alloying stage. It is found that with the advance of alloying, the alloying activation energy of the rapid alloying stage increases, and it is also proportional to the cube root of the total atom number of the system. Simulations of a Zn/Pd(111) slab model further reproduced the experimentally observed temperature dependence of the surface alloy structure: a multilayer PdZn alloy at lower temperatures and a bilayer alloy at higher temperatures. The results provide valuable insights into the fundamental mechanisms of PdZn alloy formation and offer a robust foundation for further research in catalytic applications.
relevance_reason: Development of ReaxFF parameters for Pd–Zn trained on DFT data and applied in MD simulations of diffusion-driven alloying, including slab models: (a) explicit atoms, (b) classical force-field development plus MD, and (c) both method advance and application are satisfied.

title: Calculation of thermodynamic properties of neon with  ab initio  potentials using path integral and semiclassical Monte Carlo simulations
abstract: Path integral Monte Carlo and semiclassical Monte Carlo simulations using the Feynman–Hibbs corrections to account for nuclear quantum effects were employed to calculate ten different thermodynamic properties of the noble gas neon in the isobaric-isothermal ensemble. As path integral simulations could only be carried out for small systems due to the large required computational resources, while semiclassical simulations can be performed for much larger systems, an extrapolation scheme was developed to obtain results in the quantum-mechanical and thermodynamic limits, which utilizes the similar dependence of results for thermodynamic properties on the system size in both simulation techniques. This approach yields accurate results for macroscopic thermodynamic properties and additionally allows the assessment of the validity of the Feynman–Hibbs corrections in the studied region of the phase diagram. A total of 38 state points were simulated at eight isotherms between 27.5 and 100 K, covering the liquid and supercritical regions of the phase diagram at pressures up to 90 MPa. The interactions between the neon atoms were described by highly accurate state-of-the-art ab initio potentials for both pairwise and nonadditive three-body contributions. The predicted densities and speeds of sound at the isotherms 80 and 100 K agree with the most accurate experimental data from the literature within the mutual uncertainties. At lower temperatures, our results are likely more accurate than the available experimental data for the density and speed of sound.
relevance_reason: Path-integral Monte Carlo and semiclassical Feynman–Hibbs Monte Carlo simulations of neon thermodynamics with ab initio pair and three-body potentials: (a) explicit atoms, (b) MC/PIMC on atomic configurations plus ab initio potentials, and (c) advances simulation methodology and computes thermodynamic properties, all satisfied.

title: Development and large-scale benchmarks of a protein--ligand absolute binding free energy toolkit
abstract:
arXiv:2603.22274v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Absolute binding free energy (ABFE) calculations offer a theoretically rigorous approach for predicting protein--ligand binding affinities without the scaffold constraints of relative binding free energy (RBFE) perturbations. However, broad adoption of ABFE in high-throughput hit discovery campaigns has been hindered by high computational costs and a lack of large-scale validation. Here, we present Felis, a source-available, automated, and scalable ABFE toolkit that integrates RelocationMC to enhance binding-site water sampling. Using the ByteFF25-AM1-BCC force field, ABFE calculations with Felis yielded similar average rank correlations to FEP+ RBFE across 43 benchmark systems comprising 857 ligand entries. The offset-adjusted errors were larger than those of FEP+ RBFE. In scytalone dehydratase, RelocationMC rapidly hydrated an initially dry cavity and reduced the dependence of binding free energy offsets on the initial water configuration. Across the benchmark, it reduced absolute offsets in 27 of 43 systems without a loss of aggregate predictive performance. We also evaluated sampling-length dependence and ligand ranking for a challenging KRAS(G12D) dataset containing highly charged ligands and a charged cofactor. Neither force-field parameters nor alchemical schedules were adjusted using experimental affinities from the benchmarks. These results support the use of Felis for ligand prioritization and highlight remaining sampling limitations.
relevance_reason: Development and large-scale benchmarking of an alchemical absolute binding free-energy toolkit (Felis/RelocationMC with the ByteFF25-AM1-BCC force field), which is explicit-atom MD free-energy methodology, satisfying (a), (b) and (c).

title: Molecular Modulation of the SAM-I Riboswitch Drives Global Dynamical Shifts
abstract: A surge in antimicrobial resistance in recent years has made protein-targeting antibiotics less effective against key pathogens. It is possible to expand the range of therapeutic targets by using RNA-based therapies, but it remains necessary to improve the molecular-level understanding of interactions between RNA and known and potential binders. The SAM-I riboswitch, which controls the transcriptional termination of gene expression involved in sulfur metabolism in most bacteria, is an excellent ligand target. Thus, understanding its behavior with and without ligand complexes would be helpful for drug design. Here, we studied the interactions between the SAM-I riboswitch and its natural ligand, SAM, which controls riboswitch function, and compared those to its interactions with the similar small molecule SAH, which does not control riboswitch function, and to its interactions with a potential binder JS4, identified via virtual screening. From our simulations, we deepen understanding of small molecule interactions with the SAM-I riboswitch on both a local and a distal level. The results reveal how differently ligands (SAM, SAH and JS4) can bind to and potentially induce conformational changes in the riboswitch. Our findings offer valuable insight into the molecular mechanisms underlying riboswitch RNA-ligand interactions for the design of more effective RNA-targeting therapeutics.
relevance_reason: Explicit-atom molecular dynamics simulations of the SAM-I riboswitch with SAM, SAH, and JS4 ligands to characterize binding-induced conformational and dynamical changes — satisfies (a) explicit all-atom system, (b) MD, and (c) mechanistic application.
